translation: The Verse Summary of Perfect Wisdom

academic_translation: In the language of India: Ārya-prajñāpāramitā-sañcayagāthā. In the language of Tibet: The Noble Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom. Homage to the Noble Mañjuśrī!

locked_terms.use: Noble Verse Summary of Perfect Wisdom
Noble Verse Summary of Perfect Wisdom

translation: In the language of India: Arya-prajnaparamita-sancayagatha. In the language of Tibet: The Noble Verse Summary of Perfect Wisdom. We bow to Noble Manjushri!

academic_translation: Then, in order to perfectly delight those four assemblies, the Blessed One once again taught this perfection of wisdom and at that time spoke these verses:
translation: Then, to bring great joy to the four assemblies, the Blessed One taught perfect wisdom again. At that time, he spoke these verses.

academic_translation:
Establishing supreme joy, respect, and faith,
Having cleared away obscurations and afflictions and passed beyond stains,
Listen to the perfection of wisdom of the gentle ones engaged in the welfare of beings,
In which the heroes practice their conduct.
translation: Feel great joy, respect, and trust. Clear away blocks and mental troubles to go beyond stains. Listen to the perfect wisdom of the gentle ones who work for the good of beings. This is where the heroes practice their way of living.

academic_translation:
Chapter one: Teaching the omniscience of all aspects.
However many rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa,
Producing flowers, fruits, medicinal herbs, and forests,
They all depend on the nāga king, the lord of nāgas who dwells in Anavatapta;
That is the majestic power of that lord of nāgas.
translation: Chapter one: Teaching about knowing everything in every way. Many rivers flow here in Jambudvipa. They make flowers, fruits, healing plants, and forests grow. They all depend on the serpent king. This is the lord of the serpent spirits who lives in Anavatapta. All this growth comes from the great power of that lord of the serpent spirits.

academic_translation:
Whatever Dharma the śrāvakas of the Victor teach,
Explain, and express endowed with reasoning,
As well as producing supreme noble bliss and attaining its fruit—
All of that is the power of the person of the Tathāgata.
translation: Whatever teaching the listeners of the Victorious One share, they explain it clearly with good reasons. Their words bring great joy and good results. All of this comes from the power of the Thus-Gone One.

academic_translation:
Why is this? Because whatever ways of Dharma the Victor has taught,
Those who have become disciples of the supreme human fully train in them,
And having actualized them, they teach exactly as they have trained;
They do so by the power of the Buddha, not by the power of their own strength.
translation: Why is this? Because the Victorious One has shared many ways of teaching. His students practice these ways completely. After they master them, they teach exactly what they practiced. They do this by the power of the Buddha, not by their own strength.

academic_translation:
In whom the supreme perfection of wisdom is not apprehended,
And the bodhisattva is not apprehended, nor the mind of awakening—
Having heard this, without bewilderment and without fear,
That bodhisattva practices the wisdom of the Sugatas.
translation: An awakening hero does not hold onto perfect wisdom. They do not hold onto an awakening hero or the wish to awaken. When they hear this, they are not confused or afraid. That awakening hero practices the wisdom of the Well-Gone Ones.

There is no form, no feeling, no idea, and no intention. For that person, awareness does not have even a tiny speck of a place to rest. They do not rest on any things. They practice without resting anywhere. Without grasping, they reach the awakening of the Well-Gone Ones.

academic_translation:
Just as the wandering mendicant Śreṇika, through his knowledge,
Brought about the destruction of the unapprehendable aggregates,
Any bodhisattva who understands phenomena in that way
Does not touch nirvāṇa, and abides in wisdom.
translation: A wandering seeker named Shrenika used his knowledge to destroy the heaps that no one can grasp. An awakening hero understands things in this exact same way. They do not touch the peace beyond sorrow. Instead, they stay right there in wisdom.

academic_translation:
Furthermore, examining, "What is this wisdom, and whose is it?
From where does it come?" they consider all these phenomena to be empty;
Having closely examined them, without discouragement or fear—
That bodhisattva is close to awakening.
translation: They also ask, "What is this wisdom? Whose is it? Where does it come from?" They see that all these things are empty. They look at them closely without feeling sad or afraid. That awakening hero is close to awakening.

academic_translation:
If, lacking understanding, one perceives form,
And engages with the aggregates of feeling, volition, and consciousness,
Even if they conceptualize, "These aggregates are empty," that bodhisattva
Practices with signs and lacks faith in the unborn state.
translation: Some do not truly understand. They see form. They focus on the heaps of feeling, intention, and awareness. They might even think, "These heaps are empty." But that awakening hero is still practicing with signs. They lack faith in the state that is never born.

Others do not practice in form, feeling, idea, or intention. They do not practice in awareness. They practice without staying anywhere. They do not grasp at what is called "practicing." Instead, they rely on wisdom. With a mind that knows what is never born, they touch the highest, peaceful deep calm.

academic_translation:
Whatever bodhisattva abides here thus, at peace within themselves,
Has received the prophecy from the Tathāgatas of the past;
They have no conceit, thinking, "I am in meditative equipoise," or "I have arisen."
Why is this? Because they completely understand the nature of phenomena.
translation: Any awakening hero who stays here like this is completely at peace. The Thus-Gone Ones of the past have given a prediction about them. They are not proud. They never think, "I am resting in calm," or "I have stood up." Why? Because they fully understand the nature of things.

academic_translation:
Practicing in this way, they practice the wisdom of the Sugatas,
Because they thoroughly understand that non-practice is the practice;
Whatever phenomena they practice are also not apprehended:
This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
translation: By practicing like this, they practice the wisdom of the Well-Gone Ones. They truly understand that not practicing is the real practice. They do not grasp at any of the things they practice. This is the practice of the highest perfect wisdom.

What does not exist is called non-existent. Unwise people imagine this. They think that things exist or do not exist. But existing and not existing are not real things. Any awakening hero who knows this will surely break free.

academic_translation:
Whoever here knows the five aggregates to be like an illusion,
And does not treat the illusion as one thing and the aggregates as another,
Free from diverse perceptions and practicing in perfect peace—
This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
translation: Someone here knows the five heaps are like an illusion. They do not treat the illusion as one thing and the five heaps as another. They are free from any different idea and practice in perfect peace. This is the practice of the highest perfect wisdom.

academic_translation:
One endowed with spiritual friends and endowed with special insight
Will never become afraid upon hearing the Mother of the Victors.
Whoever is endowed with bad friends and relies on others
Is like an unfired vessel that disintegrates when touched by water.
translation: Someone with a wise friend and clear insight will never be afraid. They will not be scared to hear the Mother of the Victorious Ones. But someone with a bad friend just relies on others. They are like an unbaked clay pot that falls apart when touched by water.

academic_translation:
If one asks, "Why is this one called a bodhisattva?"
Severing attachment, they desire the exhaustion of attachment to everything.
They touch the unattached awakening of the Victors;
Therefore, they obtain the name "bodhisattva."
translation: You might ask, "Why is this person called an awakening hero?" They cut off clinging. They want to completely end clinging to everything. They touch the awakening of a Victorious One, which is a state of not clinging. Because of this, they get the name awakening hero.

academic_translation:
If one asks, "Why is this one called a great being?"
Because they become the supreme among the many multitudes of sentient beings,
And sever the great views of the realm of sentient beings;
Therefore, they are proclaimed to be a great being.
translation: You might ask, "Why is this person called a great hero?" It is because they become the highest in the large crowd of living beings. They cut through the strong, wrong views in the realm of living beings. That is why they are called a great hero.

They have great giving, great intelligence, and great power. They have entered the highest Great Vehicle of the Victorious Ones. They put on the great armor and defeat the tricks of Mara. For these reasons, they are called a great hero.

academic_translation:
For example, just as a magician conjures an emanation at a crossroads,
And cuts off the tens of millions of heads of a large crowd of people—
Whatever those to be killed are like, just so the bodhisattva
Fully knows all beings to be like emanations, and has no fear.
translation: Imagine a magician creates a fake crowd at a crossroads and then cuts off all their heads. The awakening hero knows that all beings are just like those illusions. Because they know this, the awakening hero has no fear.

academic_translation:
Form and perception, feeling and volition,
And consciousness are not bound, not liberated, and do not exist.
Entering into awakening in this way without a discouraged mind,
This is the supreme armor of holy beings.
translation: Form, idea, feeling, intention, and awareness are not tied up or set free. They do not truly exist. You must enter into awakening this way without losing heart. This is the best armor for holy persons.

academic_translation:
Why is this called the Great Vehicle of Awakening?
It is that which, once mounted, brings all sentient beings beyond sorrow.
This vehicle is like space, a great immeasurable palace,
The supreme vehicle that brings about the manifest attainment of joy, happiness, and bliss.
translation: Why is this called the Great Vehicle of Awakening? Once you ride in it, it carries all living beings beyond sorrow. This vehicle is like space. It is a great palace that cannot be measured. It is the highest vehicle that brings clear joy, happiness, and bliss.

academic_translation:
Whoever mounts it, going in any direction is not apprehended;
Though taught as going to nirvāṇa, no going is apprehended.
For example, just as a dead person [Mipham, Khenrab and the Sanskrit read: a fire that has gone out] has nowhere to go,
For this reason, that person is fully proclaimed as "nirvāṇa."
translation: Whoever rides in it cannot be found going in any direction. They are taught to go to peace beyond sorrow, but no going is found. Think of a dead person who has nowhere to go. For this reason, that person is completely called peace beyond sorrow.

academic_translation:
The bodhisattva is not apprehended in the prior limit, the later limit,
Or the present; the three times are pure.
That bodhisattva is unconditioned and free from elaboration;
This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
translation: You cannot find the awakening hero in the earlier limit, the later end, or the present. The past, present and future are pure. That awakening hero is not made by causes and is free from tangled thinking. This is the practice of the highest perfect wisdom.

academic_translation:
Whenever a wise and knowing bodhisattva
Contemplates the unborn and practices in this way,
Generating great compassion without the perception of sentient beings,
This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
translation: A wise and knowing awakening hero thinks about what is never born. They practice in this way. They develop great compassion without the idea of living beings. This is the practice of the highest perfect wisdom.

academic_translation:
If one generates the perception of sentient beings and the perception of suffering,
Thinking, "I shall act for the benefit of beings and eliminate their suffering,"
One is a bodhisattva who conceptualizes self and sentient beings;
This is not the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
translation: Someone might hold the idea of living beings and the idea of suffering. They might think, "I will help beings and end their suffering." That makes them an awakening hero who only imagines a self and living beings. This is not the practice of highest perfect wisdom.
